# Chapter Ten: History Lesson

Vic sat in a chair across from the Old Priest with Sam standing looking out a window, He was bandaged and given an ample dose of pain medication. “Someone want to tell me where I am, and more important where my family is” Vic said slurring a little from the dose of pain meds. Bishop Talbot smiled a fatherly smile, “you have had a long night, you are safe we have brought you downtown to The Cathedral of St. Michael the Apostle, your family has been taken elsewhere, they are staying at St. Augustine on V St., We have some things to discuss that we would rather do so alone son.” He said shifting his gaze to Sam.

Sam came over to sit next to his friend “They are safe, I made sure of it before having us brought here, I have armed security guarding the building and it is closed off to all but the staff, I also have the tracker from earlier Edgar and a few of his friends over there as well but your wife isn’t the target, Vic it’s you and the kids they were after.” Sam said averting his friends gaze. Vic thought about a church covered with armed guards “who the hell are you people” he asked the room. His head was still spinning a little, but he took a mental pause and tried to clear it as best he could. “And what the fuck was that thing” he said in a hushed tone, thinking about the monsters in his house, the ones coming for his family. “What were those things?” he asked trying to bring his eyes to meet his friends. Sam looked at the old Bishop who nodded almost imperceptibly. “Werewolves, Vic you went head to head with Three Young Werewolves, who as I said before didn’t consider you much of a threat so they were toying with you. Had they not done that I would be visiting you at a morgue. “Sam shook his head, I’m sorry buddy, had I known they knew about you we would have had a detail at the house. It was a surprise to us. But your now safe and so is your family.

We will keep you here a few days and then move you somewhere, we are going to have to give you a new identity as well,” Sam said to his friend. Vic just stared at him, had he said werewolves, like monster movie werewolves, as if he were talking about a bear or a lion or something else that actually existed. Was this some kind of sick joke, or a test. Vic thought back to that things face, inches from his own, the smell of its breath and the look in its eyes. That was no mask, it had been real. He felt off balance, not quite sure where his line of reality ended and fantasy began, this incident had shaken his view of the world right down to its core. “Werewolves, are you fucking series Sam?” he looked up at his friend trying to search his eyes, he was never good at lying and unfortunately, he was not, Shit, werewolves, was this even possible, what’s next vampires or hey ghosts even he thought to himself a small chuckle escaping his lips

“This isn’t funny Vic, I am serious, we have hunted packs like this for ages, unfortunately due to your unique family history, they are now also looking for you” Sam said a little edge to his voice. The bishop stood up and laid a hand on his partner, why not let Mr., Handy rest for a bit, we are laying quite a bit at his feet and he still needs to heal, everyone is safe, Sam can you show your friend to his room?”

Sam nodded, “come on buddy, let’s get you some rest.” He said gently taking Vic by the uninjured arm. They walked deeper into the building leaving the Bishop to content with other matters. “Sam, are you serious about this?” Vic said a pleading entering his voice as he spoke to his friend, he wanted to hear a lie, he wanted to know that this couldn’t be possible that it was all something in his mind.” Sam nodded, “It is true Vic, I am as serious as a heart attack, you need to come to terms with this, they are after you and your kids my friend” Vic stopped and looked at his friend “Why Sam, why the kids, why me” Sam shook his head, “That is a longer story and we will tell you, but let’s get you some rest, it’s going to be a long one and some of it is going to be a little hard to believe” he said moving his friend along the hall “Vic laughed, his ribbed feeling like they were going to come apart when he did “More difficult them werewolves” he said and Sam just looked at him and nodded.

Vic let himself be led to one of the back bedrooms, the pills kicking in and taking effect, he could feel himself getting sleepy. “Vic, I promise we will go over it when you wake, we will be in the next room if you need anything “he said laying Vic down and then heading for the door. Vic said something unintelligible and then he was out like a light. Vic shut the door and went back to the main area where the Bishop was “We need to tell him everything Sir, He needs to know the danger he is in” Sam said to the older man. Bishop Talbot nodded “I agree, when he wakes up, let’s see if he notices the gifts I left” Sam just cocked his head and then looked towards the display case, the sword and knives were missing “Sir, you can’t let him touch those without at least a warning” The Bishop gave him a stern look “I can and I will, he needs to know what he is dealing with and this is the quickest route” Sam just shook his head and wished his friend wouldn’t touch the items that were probably somewhere displayed in the room, he needed time to tell him everything before he touched any of them, his mind was fragile enough.

Sam went off to bed and ensured he said a prayer for his friend before going to sleep. Guards patrolled outside to ensure the building was safe and the Bishop was already on the phone with his people in Rome. IT was going to be a long day tomorrow

Alfonso

Vic awoke around 5 AM and looked around sleepily, the room was silent as the building seemed to be. He could hear some traffic on the streets but this early, it wasn’t much. He sat up on the edge of the bed and checked his wounds, they hurt like hell, He noticed the pill bottles next to his bed and tried to read them, his sight was still blurry with sleep, so he took one of each and swallowed them dry, he hoped one was a pain killer.

Apparently one was and within 15 minutes he could feel the pain subside a bit allowing him to get up off the bed, He still hurt but it was manageable. He limped over to the door and tried it locked, typical he didn’t think he was a prisoner but nor was he going to be allowed to wander around unescorted either. He spied the bathroom and limped in to relieve himself. Getting a look in the mirror he could see a lot of bruising on his face, though some of the swelling had gone down a little, he still looked like hell. As he came out of the bathroom he spied the weapons on the table near the window, it was a sword and two long knives, they glinted with the early morning light coming in from the street lights that hadn’t yet shut off. Vic shuffled over to examine them. Not sure why they would be lying around like that.

He stared at the weapons for a moment and then picked up the dagger.

It was dark through the window and Vic could see his reflection, but it was not his, the face was younger with longer hair. “I fear I might not be ready” said a voice he didn’t know in accented English “My son, you have been trained and though this is your first solo mission, you have done this before, you are ready “said a voice over his shoulder, Alfonso didn’t feel ready, in fact he felt scared “How many have been seen?” he asked the old priest. Father Marquis had been the priest of Jamestown just going on 2 years now, but he had been put here by the order. He knew at least one pack of wolves had come over to the new world looking for better hunting grounds away from persecution. And with the influx of settlers and the existing tribes of Indians, they had found it. Alfonso knew he had a duty and he being only one of two hunters in the new world had a duty and responsibility to the church and his oath. He hung his head “I will father, I will complete the task given” He said thinking he would not live through it, the cold radiated off of the window and sent a chill through Alfonso, who closed the lapels on his leather coat and cinched it with the leather string. He had been a child when his uncle had introduced him to the order and he had been on several hunts in England and Ireland but never alone, this would be his first solo mission and he had doubts.

Vic dropped the dagger and stumbled back, “What the hell” he said to the empty room looking around expecting to see a priest and then looked in the mirror hanging near him and saw his reflection, not the reflection of the young man whom he had just been. He stared at the dagger, somehow he had lived someone else’s memory, how was this possible he thought to himself moving closer to study the daggers and sword. Obviously they had been put there for this purpose, but by who Vic thought he knew, The Bishop, but what was the bishop selling. Vic shook his head still trying to grasp what had just happened. He remembered every detail, every thought and fear that the young man Alfonso had, it was as if he felt them too and understood. He knew that Alfonso had been a wolf hunter for the order and that he was just given a mission and he had doubts, he had felt the man’s fear and his excitement as if they were his own. Vic sat for a while staring at the dagger, trying to resolve his feelings of fear and curiosity, he wanted to try again but was afraid of what he would see. For 30 minutes he sat there staring at the weapons, rubbing his palms as he reviewed what could possibly happen, had this been a real person? Vic thought it had, the era was not one he knew well, but it seemed authentic, the room had looked like it would have belonged in Jamestown from some of the museums he had visited as a child and what little he knew.

Finally, his curiosity won out and he reached for the dagger.

Alfonso crouched in the woods outside of the settlement. He could see his breath coming out in clouds as he slowly inhaled and exhaled. He didn’t move a muscle as he listened to the wilderness talk to him. He had been taught since a young age how to hunt in the woods, and whether it was deer or wolves,

he knew how to track prey, the woods were eerily silent, he knew the wolves were out there, and that the natural creatures of the woods sensed them, they would burrow and hide from the creatures as they were not natural and would offend those that belonged in the wilderness. He heard nothing for a long time as he strained for any sound, then he heard it, a twig snap not far off to his left. “Bakhzataa” he whispered the Aramaic word for sight and suddenly the woods lightened and he could see the heat auras of everything within his sightline, and there not far off was the profile of a large animal standing on two legs, he had found one of the wolves. He tensed but didn’t move as the creature was facing away from him and upwind, he had gotten lucky. Alfonso slowly drew his sword and one of the daggers he could feel the heft of both as he moved towards the creature silently, each step bringing it closer. The sword glowed a blue hue that brightened with each step,

Alfonso knew the creature could not see the light as it was only seen by the wielder of the weapon as his father had been and his father before him. The light did not blind or obscure his vision but definitely the closer he got the more it shined for the wielder. Alfonso was 10 steps from the creature and gripped the weapons tighter “RPap” he said uttering the Aramaic word for Movement and with the burst of speed it gave he lunged forward. As soon as he stood up the creature whirled around hearing the movement of the earth around him. He began to let out a snarl as the fast moving Alfonso uttered “bkhyl” meaning strength and lobbed the creatures head off with one fell swing of the blade. The head fell from the creature and rolled into the underbrush as the body stood there a moment seeming to not know it had been dealt a killing blow, then it tipped and fell to the ground with a meaty sound against the dirt and leaves. Alfonso felt the speed and strength flow away from his body as his sight remained.

Vic took his hand away from the dagger, sweat had creased his brow and his shirt stuck to his body, he leaned back breathing heavy as he thought about what had just happened. Like before he had experienced it through this person. That had been amazing he felt the earth beneath his feet and the feel of the blade as it lobbed the head of the wolf off and the victory that Alfonso felt coursed through him like the afterglow of an orgasm. That was incredible he thought as he leaned back on the couch and composed himself. He looked over to discover it had only been a few seconds, but he had been tracking the beast for at least two hours, how was this possible. It was like time was different when he touched the blade. “Interesting” he said to the empty room.

He contemplated the dagger on the table, He felt he was learning from it, like reading a book only fuller and richer in content and meaning. He couldn’t fully comprehend or put into words what it was, but he was gleaning an incredible amount of information on multiple levels. He shook his head, he wanted more and hobbled over to the table, he looked down at the dagger for a moment, then reached out to touch the hilt.

Alfonso stood there with the sword over his head “Like this uncle” the young man said unsteadily holding the blade. The older man stood near him judging his stance “Higher with the blade Alfonso” the old man said the sun shining off of his steel grey head and highlighting the scar that ran the length of his face and over a milky white eye, the other one though shined blue and fiery as he gauged his nephew’s sword stance, he took a rod and hit his back, straighter and get that sword up, you will require the swing, the power comes from the shoulders not your arms young man.

Vic took his hand off the dagger and shook his head, “What the hell was that” he said to no one, one second he was in the woods with an older man and now he was a young teen, It was like a random vision, or was it, He stood unsteadily on his feet, feeling the pain and picked up the sword, but no vision came as he raised it over his head, straightening his back and mimicking what the young man had learned, so had he. He put the sword down and stared at it. Was it a teaching tool or something else, he didn’t know but he knew he had to see more.

Over the next 4 hours he sat there with the dagger cradled in his lap and his eyes closed as he relived the young Alfonso’s sword training, from early teen to adulthood, it spanned a decade of training in just 5 hours. He finally opened his eyes and put the dagger down, he looked at the clock and couldn’t believe it had only been 5 hours, it had felt like years as he had gone through training after training through the eyes of this man. He stood and picked up the sword and dagger knowing it would not trigger a vision and went through a warmup exercise wielding both as competently as if he himself had trained on them for years. He had used the vision like one would use a movie or a video game, as a way of escaping, he had been almost beaten and almost killed, he needed to protect himself and more importantly his family, this gave him not only a chance but an escape from his pain and humiliation of the night before.

He knew every move and swing both weapons could perform and within the next few minutes as best as his hurting body could do performed a series of moves flawlessly and then smiled, he knew how to use these weapons in 5 hours he had grown from ignorance to a veritable master of the blades. How was this possible he thought as he pushed himself through another series of moves with the weapons? He knew the moves and he performed them as if he had practiced with the weapons every day. It was amazing he thought, it was unbelievable yet here it was. He put the weapons down as he shoulders and legs began to protest at him. He shuffled over to the bedside and grabbed another handful of pills, he dry swallowed them wincing and then sat on the bed until they took effect. He had read the labels this time and ensured he was taking the pain pills and anti-inflammatories, but leaving the others that would make him drowsy, he didn’t need sleep, he needed answers.

He banged on the door and after a few moments an armed man in tactical gear opened it and looked indifferently at the excited bandaged man on the other side. “Take me to your leader” was all Vic said, the man gave him an are you serious look and then began to lead the way down the hall, Vic hobbling along behind him following.
